title: Jailer 2's Hindi Version Beats Leo's Lifetime in One Week as Worldwide Gross Tops Rs 576 Crore
excerpt: The Rajinikanth sequel closed its first Hindi week at Rs 28.25 crore, past Leo's Rs 27.17 crore Hindi lifetime, while its worldwide week-one gross reached Rs 576.45 crore.
body:
• Jailer 2's Hindi version collected Rs 28.25 crore in its first week, surpassing the Rs 27.17 crore Hindi lifetime of Vijay's Leo, according to Sacnilk figures reported by Filmibeat.
  • Worldwide, the film grossed Rs 576.45 crore in week one, The Hollywood Reporter India reported — the fastest Tamil film to cross Rs 300 crore.
  • Its four-day opening of about Rs 402 crore was the biggest ever for a Kollywood film, with a record $18.70 million overseas weekend that also passed Leo.
  • The Hindi run is doing this without the major national chains — the sequel had already doubled the original Jailer's Hindi lifetime by its first weekend.

Rajinikanth's Jailer 2 has cleared another Vijay benchmark — this time in the Hindi market. The film's Hindi version earned Rs 3 crore on day seven, taking its first-week total to Rs 28.25 crore and past the Rs 27.17 crore lifetime Hindi collection of Thalapathy Vijay's Leo, according to Sacnilk figures reported by Filmibeat.

A worldwide week one of Rs 576 crore

The Hindi milestone is one line in a much larger ledger. The Hollywood Reporter India put the film's week-one worldwide gross at Rs 576.45 crore, making it the fastest Tamil film to cross Rs 300 crore. The opening had already set the Kollywood record: about Rs 402 crore worldwide in four days, ahead of Coolie's Rs 371 crore, with India contributing Rs 224 crore.

"The opening had already set the Kollywood record: about Rs 402 crore worldwide in four days, ahead of Coolie's Rs 371 crore, with India contributing Rs 224 crore."

Overseas, the film posted $18.70 million over the extended weekend — the biggest international opening for a Kollywood film, surpassing Leo's $18 million at historical exchange rates, Pinkvilla reported. The Middle East led, with the UAE becoming one of its biggest-ever opening markets for a Tamil film; North America contributed $4.14 million, with Australia, the United Kingdom, Malaysia and Singapore also strong. Trackers say $25 million overseas is now certain, with $28–29 million realistic if holds stay robust.

Why the Hindi number matters

Dubbed Tamil films rarely build a real Hindi market. Jailer 2's Hindi version opened at Rs 3.15 crore, dipped, then climbed through the weekend to Rs 5.25 crore on day four — Rs 15.65 crore in four days, already more than double the original Jailer's full Hindi lifetime of about Rs 7.5 crore. It has done this without a release in the major national chains, PVR INOX and Cinepolis among them, which makes the week-one Rs 28.25 crore a single-screen and regional-chain achievement.

https://x.com/AbGeorge_/status/2112907134169919658

The records have been falling in sequence — Kerala fell to the film in seven days earlier this week. Directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, the sequel returns Rajinikanth as 'Tiger' Muthuvel Pandian alongside Ramya Krishnan, with S. J. Suryah, Mithun Chakraborty, Suraj Venjaramoodu and Vidya Balan joining the cast and cameos by Hrithik Roshan and Vijay Sethupathi. The second weekend now decides whether the film's sights move from Leo's marks to the all-time Tamil lifetime chart.
